title: HOA fined my Halloween decorations
author: Storytime
hook: My HOA fined me two hundred dollars for my Halloween decorations. So I read every single page of the rules.
story: Every October I go all out for Halloween. Skeletons, fog machine, a twelve foot spider on the roof. The kids on our street love it. This year, the day after I put it up, I got a letter from the HOA president, Mr. Pratt. A two hundred dollar fine. Decorations exceeding approved height. Mr. Pratt is the guy who wrote half the rules himself. So I asked for a copy of the full rule book. All ninety pages. And I read every single one. Page sixty-two. Holiday decorations must be removed within fourteen days after the holiday. The fine is fifty dollars per day. Now, here's the thing. Mr. Pratt has had Christmas lights on his house since twenty nineteen. All year round. Every day. They're on right now. I did the math. Almost seven years. That's about two thousand five hundred days, at fifty dollars a day. I printed the rule, the photos with dates, and the math, and I brought it to the HOA meeting. I read it out loud. The room went silent. Then the treasurer started laughing. Mr. Pratt said rules are rules, but not like that. The board voted. My fine was canceled. His wasn't. Now he's asking me to drop it. Should I?
caption: page sixty-two changed everything 🎃 #storytime
sound: a spooky but playful Halloween beat at very low volume
why: Posted right before Halloween, HOA stories are a favorite petty revenge genre, the rules he wrote himself are the setup, and the satisfying reversal plus the final question drive comments.

title: Free babysitting for my sister
author: Storytime
hook: I babysat my sister's kids every Saturday for a year, for free. Then I saw her payment app.
story: My older sister Rachel got divorced last year. She has two kids, and she started working Saturdays. She asked if I could watch them, just until she figured things out. Of course I said yes. I love those kids. Every Saturday, eight in the morning to six at night. For a whole year. I never asked for a cent. She'd sometimes leave me a frozen pizza and call it payment. Last month, I was at her place, and she asked me to send her ex-husband a photo from her phone. A picture of the kids. When I opened her phone, her payment app was open. And there was a payment from her ex. Eighty dollars. The note said, Saturday childcare. I scrolled. Every single Saturday. For a year. Eighty dollars. She had been telling him she paid a professional babysitter, and he'd been covering half. That's over four thousand dollars, for the babysitting I did for free. I asked her about it. She said, it's not stealing, it's child support, and that I'd do it anyway because I'm family. So I told her I'm charging her for next Saturday. Eighty dollars. Now my mom says I'm being petty. Am I wrong?
caption: the babysitter she was paying was ME 💸 #storytime
sound: a slow, slightly tense lo-fi beat at very low volume
why: Family taking advantage of free help is extremely relatable, the frozen pizza payment sets up the reveal, and an am I wrong ending gets both sides commenting.

title: My subletter changed the locks
author: Storytime
hook: I sublet my apartment for the summer. When I came back, my key didn't work anymore.
story: Last summer I got a three month internship in another city. So I sublet my apartment to a girl named Brooke. She seemed perfect. She paid on time. She even sent me photos of my plants. On September first, I came home. My key didn't work. I knocked. A man I'd never seen opened the door. He said, who are you? I said, I live here. He said, no, I live here. I'm renting it from Brooke. She had changed the locks, and listed my apartment online, as hers. She had been renting it to three different people, a week at a time, all summer. The plant photos were old pictures from my own social media. I called my landlord, ready to scream. And he said something I didn't expect. He said, I know. I've been getting the rent from her every month. Double. Brooke had been paying him extra, so he'd never ask questions. And now he said the apartment was hers, because she was the one paying. Part two, if you want to know what was in the lease.
caption: my plants were fine. my apartment was not 🔑 #storytime
sound: a suspenseful, ticking thriller sound at very low volume
why: Sublet and housing disputes are trending in multipart storytime series, the plant photos are a planted clue, and the landlord twist plus the lease cliffhanger set up a part two.
